outcome: Explain how breaking problems down and hiding detail helps model the real world and solve problems.
Explain the benefits of splitting a program into subprograms.
Follow and write algorithms as flowcharts, pseudocode or code using sequence, selection, loops, iteration, input, processing and output.
Explain why variables and constants are needed and use them with strings, records and 1D/2D arrays in algorithms.
Use arithmetic, relational and logical operators (including modulus, integer division, exponentiation) in algorithms.
Work out an algorithm's output for given data and use a trace table to track variable values.
Distinguish syntax, logic and runtime errors and find and fix logic errors in algorithms.
Describe how bubble sort, merge sort, linear search and binary search work.
Use reasoning and test data to judge whether an algorithm is fit for purpose and efficient.
Apply AND, OR and NOT in truth tables with up to three inputs.
Explain that all data and instructions are stored as binary and work out how many states a pattern of given length can hold.
Explain how unsigned integers and two's complement signed integers are represented and manipulated.
Convert between denary and 8-bit binary, both unsigned and signed.
Add two positive binary patterns and apply logical and arithmetic binary shifts.
Explain overflow when a value needs more bits than are available.
Explain why hexadecimal is used and convert between hexadecimal and binary.
Explain how characters are encoded using 7-bit ASCII.
Explain how bitmap images are stored using pixels, resolution and colour depth.
Explain how analogue sound is stored in binary using amplitude, sample rate, bit depth and sample interval.
Describe the limits of binary representation when the number of bits is fixed.
Use binary storage units from bit to tebibyte and write expressions for file sizes and capacity needs.
Explain why compression is needed and how lossless and lossy methods work.
Explain the stored program concept and the roles of RAM, CPU parts, clock and buses in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
Explain the role of secondary storage and how magnetic, optical and solid state devices store data.
Explain what an embedded system is and what it is used for.
Explain the purpose of an operating system: file, process, peripheral and user management.
Explain the purpose of utility software such as backup, defragmentation, compression and anti-malware.
Explain why robust software matters and how audit trails and code reviews find vulnerabilities.
Describe the features and uses of low-level and high-level languages.
Explain how an interpreter and a compiler translate code differently.
Explain why computers are connected in networks.
Describe LANs and WANs.
Explain how the internet is structured using IP addressing and routers.
Explain how wired and wireless connections differ in speed, range, latency and bandwidth.
Use bits-per-second units to calculate file size, transmission rate and time.
Explain why network protocols are needed and the roles of Ethernet, Wi-Fi, TCP/IP, HTTP(S), FTP and email protocols.
Describe how the four TCP/IP layers handle data across a network.
Describe the features of bus, star and mesh topologies.
Explain why network security matters, how penetration testing finds weaknesses, and how access control, physical security and firewalls protect.
Explain the environmental effects of digital devices: energy use, manufacture, replacement and disposal.
Explain the ethical and legal issues of collecting and using personal data.
Explain the ethical and legal issues of AI, machine learning and robotics, such as bias, safety and liability.
Describe how copyright, patents, trademarks and licences protect computer systems and software.
Describe malware types and how hackers use technical weaknesses and social engineering.
Describe protection methods: anti-malware, encryption, acceptable use policies, backup and recovery.
Use decomposition and abstraction to analyse and solve programming problems.
Read, write, analyse and refine programs in a high-level language.
Convert flowcharts and pseudocode algorithms into programs.
Use layout, indentation, comments, meaningful names and white space to make programs readable and maintainable.
Identify, locate and correct logic, syntax and runtime errors.
Use reasoning and test data to judge a program's fitness for purpose and efficiency.
Identify and explain the structural components of programs, from constants and variables to subprograms and input/output.
Write programs using sequence, selection, loops, iteration and single entry/exit points.
Use primitive types and 1D/2D structured types (string, array, record) appropriately.
Use variables and constants appropriately in programs.
Write programs that manipulate strings: length, position, substrings, case conversion.
Write programs that accept and respond sensibly to user input.
Write programs that read from and write to CSV text files.
Explain why validation is needed and implement length, presence, range and pattern checks.
Explain why authentication is needed and implement ID/password and lookup checks.
Write programs using arithmetic operators.
Write programs using relational operators.
Write programs using logical operators.
Use built-in, library and user-written procedures and functions.
Write functions that return values and procedures that do not, with or without parameters.
Explain the difference between global and local variables and use each appropriately.
